findings.claim: Key fact: 'Reflex arcs bypass the brain, making responses faster.' The conclusion and a flashcard repeat 'bypass the brain'.
findings.truth: The spec says reflex actions 'do not involve the conscious part of the brain'. Some reflexes are routed through the brain, so 'bypass the brain' is an over-generalisation. The main paragraph (n10) already states it correctly, and the spec sets no cranial-reflex example, so no marks are at risk here.
findings.evidence: spec 4.5.2.1: 'Reflex actions are automatic and rapid; they do not involve the conscious part of the brain.'

findings.claim: Type 1 diabetes tooltip: 'It is usually genetic and is treated with insulin injections.'
findings.truth: Type 1 diabetes is not usually inherited; it is an autoimmune loss of insulin-producing cells, with only a genetic predisposition. A student who writes 'Type 1 is inherited' gains nothing. The visible body text already says it is not linked to lifestyle, so the tooltip is the only wrong surface.
findings.evidence: spec 4.5.3.2 states only that the pancreas fails to produce sufficient insulin and that it is treated with insulin injections; it gives no genetic cause

findings.claim: Knowledge check 3 and flashcards 9 and 14 test glucagon, while the article puts the whole glucagon paragraph and its key fact inside a higher-only block.
findings.truth: Glucagon is Higher tier only in this spec, so the article gating is right but the questions are not flagged. A Foundation student meets questions on material the lesson has hidden from them. Prefix '(Higher tier)' on the three items.
findings.evidence: spec 4.5.3.2: '(HT only) If the blood glucose concentration is too low, the pancreas produces the hormone glucagon...' and '(HT only) ... explain how glucagon interacts with insulin in a negative feedback cycle'

findings.claim: Practice question 4 (interactions of oestrogen and the pituitary hormones), practice question 5, knowledge check 2 and flashcards 10, 11 and 12 (all IVF) carry no tier flag, although the article gates the fertility-treatment section in a higher-only block.
findings.truth: Both the menstrual-cycle interactions and the use of hormones to treat infertility are Higher tier only in this spec. Prefix '(Higher tier)' on the six items.
findings.evidence: spec 4.5.3.4: '(HT only) Students should be able to explain the interactions of FSH, oestrogen, LH and progesterone, in the control of the menstrual cycle'; spec heading 4.5.3.6 'The use of hormones to treat infertility (HT only)'

findings.claim:
The IVF bullet opens with

findings.truth: Malformed markup, not a wrong fact. It sits inside the higher-only block that this check leaves in place, so an edit here would be a structural change with no factual gain. Worth a tidy pass on the unit, not a content fix.

findings.claim: The higher-only block wraps only the menstrual-cycle key fact, while the ungated bullets above already teach the Higher-tier interactions ('At high levels, it stimulates LH release and inhibits FSH').
findings.truth: The gating is inconsistent in both directions: a mostly both-tier revision summary is hidden from Foundation, and the Higher-tier interaction detail is shown to them. Foundation students still get every hormone role from the ungated bullets, so nothing examinable is lost; sorting it out means rewriting the key fact, which is a judgement call rather than a correction.

findings.claim: Many plants and some animals (e.g. bacteria, starfish) can reproduce asexually.
findings.truth: Bacteria are not animals. Reworded so bacteria stand as their own group and starfish remain the animal example.
findings.evidence: settled fact; spec 4.6.1.1 names bacteria separately from animals

findings.claim: A higher-only div opens before the 'Punnett Squares and Genetic Diagrams' heading and closes at the end of the lesson, so Punnett squares, the cystic fibrosis worked example, polydactyly, embryo screening and sex determination were all badged Higher Tier.
findings.truth: All of that is core content for both tiers. Foundation students saw none of it while still being asked about cystic fibrosis, polydactyly and XX/XY in the practice questions, knowledge checks and flashcards. The wrapper is removed. (This is the same defect the Combined Science Biology Paper 2 unit carried.)

findings.truth: A truncated generation-failure placeholder. It also names the wrong spec section: genetic engineering is 4.6.2.4; 4.6.4 is Classification of living organisms. Replaced with a plain 83-character description.

findings.claim: All six practice questions read 'Cannot generate practice questions without specification content', with mark schemes 'Content requirements not available'. Items 5 and 6 are typed '9 marks - Evaluate' and '12 marks - Extended'.
findings.truth: The lesson shipped with no usable practice at all, and with two question formats this board never sets. Six replacement questions written from the spec content the lesson teaches: genetic engineering, GM crops, insulin from GM bacteria, the Higher-tier steps of genetic engineering (flagged), a 6-mark GM discussion and competition in a community.
findings.evidence: spec 2.2 Assessments: Paper 2 is 1 hour 45 minutes and 100 marks, with multiple choice, structured, closed short answer and open response questions; extended response tops out at 6 marks

findings.claim: Key takeaways: 'Complete specification content needed for accurate lesson generation', 'Genetic engineering and ecology are interconnected topics in modern biology', 'Exam questions require specific examples and balanced evaluation'.
findings.truth: Three generation-failure placeholders that teach nothing. Replaced with takeaways on genetic engineering, ecosystems and interdependence, and trophic levels.

findings.claim: A higher-only div wraps the paragraph on energy loss between trophic levels, so it is badged Higher Tier on the page.
findings.truth: Trophic levels and the transfer of biomass are separate-Biology content, which this qualification includes, but the spec marks none of 4.7.4 as Higher tier only. Foundation students must learn it, so the wrapper is removed.

findings.truth: The steps of genetic engineering are Higher tier only in this spec, so the article gating is right and the questions need the same flag. Prefix '(Higher tier)' on the three items.
findings.evidence: spec 4.6.2.4: '(HT only) Students should be able to describe the main steps in the process of genetic engineering' and '(HT only) In genetic engineering: enzymes are used to isolate the required gene...'

findings.claim: glossary_terms is an empty array, although the article defines fifteen terms with <dfn> tags and every other lesson in the unit ships a glossary.
findings.truth: Another symptom of the same failed generation run. Authoring fifteen glossary entries is a content job rather than a fact correction, so it is left for the rebuild.

findings.claim: Evidence for evolution comes from fossils, antibiotic-resistant bacteria and comparative anatomy.
findings.truth: The spec names only fossils and antibiotic resistance in bacteria. Comparative anatomy is correct biology and would not be penalised, so it stays.
findings.evidence: spec 4.6.3.4: 'describe the evidence for evolution including fossils and antibiotic resistance in bacteria'

findings.claim: Unit level. These eight lessons are the Combined Science Biology Paper 2 lessons, and this is the only unit in the separate-sciences subject that covers topics 5 to 7. Large parts of the biology-only content are therefore taught nowhere.
findings.truth: Missing: the eye and accommodation (4.5.2.3); control of body temperature (4.5.2.4); water and nitrogen balance, the kidney, ADH and dialysis (4.5.3.3); plant hormones and their uses, with required practical 8 (4.5.4); DNA structure and protein synthesis (4.6.1.5); cloning (4.6.1.3); the work of Darwin, Wallace and Mendel and speciation (4.6.3.1 to 4.6.3.3); required practical 9 is used but never named; decomposition with required practical 10 (4.7.2.3); impact of environmental change (4.7.2.4); pyramids of biomass, the 10 % transfer figure and efficiency calculations (4.7.4.2, 4.7.4.3); and the whole of food production, food security, sustainable fisheries and biotechnology (4.7.5). Options: (a) build the missing lessons, which is roughly the five extra lessons the Combined unit wrongly carried, or (b) accept the gap and say so on the unit page. Recommend (a) - a separate-science student sitting this paper is examined on all of it.
findings.evidence: spec sections listed above, each headed '(biology only)'; brief _queue.json confirms separate-sciences AQA has only six units, so no other unit covers topics 5 to 7

summary: Board anchors verified in the spec: two papers, each 1 hour 45 minutes, 100 marks, 50 %, Foundation and Higher, Paper 2 = topics 5 to 7. No lesson makes an exam-structure claim, and required practical 7 (reaction time) is correctly numbered for this qualification. Every Punnett-square ratio and probability recomputes correctly (3:1, 25 %, 50 %), and all forty knowledge-check answer keys and match orders are right. Two defects dominate: lesson 7 shipped from a failed generation run with six placeholder practice questions (two of them typed 9 marks and 12 marks), three placeholder takeaways, a truncated description naming the wrong spec section and an empty glossary; and lesson 5 wrapped Punnett squares, inherited disorders, embryo screening and sex determination in a higher-only div, hiding both-tier core content from Foundation. Also fixed: a higher-only wrapper on trophic-level energy transfer (biology only, but not Higher only), bacteria called animals, a Type 1 diabetes tooltip calling it genetic, and twelve Higher-tier-only questions and flashcards left untagged next to article text that gates them. The unit-level ADJUDICATE is the real issue: these are the Combined lessons, so most of the biology-only Paper 2 content is taught nowhere in this subject.
